statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. All 24 published hours fall inside the scheduled weekend halt of CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD, so no pathological Nasdaq-100 price path can form within the window, while the rate, energy and diplomatic backdrop behind elevated Stress stays unresolved.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold for every published hour because no tradable Nasdaq-100 venue exists before Sunday 22:00Z, which is roughly 21 hours beyond the final slot. Elevated Stress describes a 5.18% 10-year yield, $92.44 WTI and an unaccepted Iranian Hormuz proposal rather than any observed mean-reversion failure. Reopen gap risk falls outside this window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 inside the scheduled CME weekend closure after an orderly Friday advance; Tail at its floor with Stress elevated on a post-GFC-high 10-year yield, $92 crude and unresolved Hormuz diplomacy
body: Friday's session closed in orderly, two-sided fashion and nothing has traded since. Cash NDX finished 30,608.14, up 0.42% or 129.28 points, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.19% below the session high, while NQ Dec-26 last printed 30,921.75, up 0.50%, within a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range and roughly 0.24% below its own high. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 in a 14.68-15.94 range. All three major US averages posted weekly gains: the Dow rose 0.93% to 51,828.62 and snapped a three-week losing streak, the S&P 500 rose 0.51% to 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.48% to 27,068.72. Retracements occurred repeatedly through the session and the index did not hold an extreme into the close, so none of the mean-reversion-failure amplifiers were present when the tape stopped. CME equity-index futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, roughly twenty-one hours past the final published hour, so every slot in this assessment sits inside a scheduled closure with no tradable venue. That is why Tail is held near its floor rather than inferred from Friday's mildly positive tone. The environment behind elevated Stress is genuinely unresolved. The 10-year Treasury yield stands at 5.18%, its highest level since the global financial crisis, with H.15 for September 24 showing the 2-year at 4.87%. The Federal Reserve raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on September 16 and futures price roughly a 69% probability of a further increase at the October 28 meeting. WTI settled at $92.44, down 2.29% in a $91.51-$94.75 range, and Brent at $104.32, down 2.14%, after Iran's foreign minister proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade, releasing roughly $12bn in frozen assets and ending hostilities across the region. Washington has not accepted those terms and Secretary Rubio declined to describe the talks as a breakthrough, so the Hormuz closure and its supply premium remain in place. Friday's leadership was dispersed rather than one-way, with Microsoft closing at its highest level of the year while Meta fell 3.3%, which argues against aligned breadth as a Tail amplifier. The coming week carries August PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and September payrolls on Friday. Those are forward checkpoints that raise Stress and shape Confidence; under this contract they do not by themselves raise Tail before a price path is observed. Shared Finviz context was read and is roughly half an hour old, well inside the 90-minute freshness window, but reports collectionStatus partial with both its futures and calendar sections unavailable; its latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor readings were used only as non-real-time confirmation of Friday's dispersed leadership, and every level quoted above comes from a primary source verified directly during this run.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 published hours the Claude state ranged between Tail 9 and 22 and never approached the block threshold. The overnight and early European stretch held Tail at 18 in normal conditions, four trend-up prints appeared between 06:00Z and 11:00Z as the index worked higher, and the US cash session settled into mixed conditions at Tail 18-21. The 13:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed. The final five hours fell to Tail 12, 10, 10, 9 and 9 as CME futures settled into the weekend closure and no tradable price path remained. Stress ranged between 46 and 59, holding in the mid-50s through the European and US cash hours before easing to 46 by the last published hour, and Confidence held between 85 and 88 throughout.
outlookSummary: The entire published window falls inside the scheduled CME weekend closure: futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, roughly twenty-one hours past the final slot. Tail is held between 7 and 10 for all 24 hours because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, and none of the inherited amplifiers, shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, or an index pinned near an extreme, can be observed while every Nasdaq-100 venue is shut. Stress eases from 45 to 43 through the deepest part of the closure and firms to 50 by the final hour as the PCE, ISM and payrolls week and a live October rate decision approach. Confidence decays from 84 to 70 across the window because later hours sit progressively further from the verified Friday evidence set, while the exchange calendar anchoring the low Tail stays certain. Weekend geopolitical or diplomatic developments, above all a US response to Iran's Hormuz proposal, would transmit only as headlines within this window; their earliest possible price expression is the Sunday reopen, which lies outside it.

forecastDetail.comment: No Nasdaq-100 venue trades in this hour. NQ Dec-26 last printed 30,921.75 (+0.50%) at the Friday 21:00Z settle after cash NDX closed 30,608.14 (+0.42%) inside a two-sided 30,413.59-30,667.56 range, leaving Tail at its floor and Stress elevated on 5.18% 10-year yields and $92 crude.

Second hour of the scheduled closure with nothing repriced since the settle. None of the inherited Tail amplifiers, shallow pullbacks, failed retracements or extension from an extreme, can be observed while every Nasdaq-100 venue is shut, and Friday's tape retraced repeatedly into the close.

Tail eases to its floor as distance from the last tradable print grows while the exchange calendar stays certain. Stress holds at 44 on the rate backdrop: H.15 shows the 2-year at 4.87% and the 10-year at 5.18%, the highest long-end level since the global financial crisis.

On a weekday this hour would carry the Asian handover into Europe; this weekend there is no handover to price. Headlines arriving now accumulate as unpriced information whose earliest possible expression is the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, well outside this window.

Energy is the clearest weekend variable. WTI settled $92.44 (-2.29%) and Brent $104.32 (-2.14%) after Iran floated a phased Hormuz reopening, but the Strait stays closed under the US naval blockade and no change can be scored on price until a venue reopens.

Stress eases to 43, its low for this window, as the quietest stretch of the closure begins with no venue, no scheduled release and no confirmed diplomatic step due. Tail remains at its floor because a closed market cannot produce a pathological price path.
